headline: Ferry and Camping Reservation Check
reservation: Public-ferry tickets are separate from camping reservations. Check current Peddocks camping availability; camping and visitor services are not currently offered on Grape Island. Confirm transport and permitted access for each island before travel.

days.title: Harbor History and Views

stops.name: Georges Island
stops.detail: Explore the granite corridors and dark tunnels of the historic Fort Warren.

stops.name: Spectacle Island
stops.detail: Walk the perimeter trails for the highest elevation in the harbor and skyline views.

days.driving: Walking and ferry only. No inter-island public ferry is currently operating; choose Georges or Spectacle for the day, or return to Boston and purchase a separate round-trip ticket for the second island.
days.note: Last ferries depart early; check the daily schedule at the dock to avoid being stranded.

days.title: Outer Island Solitude

stops.name: Peddocks Island
stops.detail: Visit the ruins of Fort Andrews and walk the unique sand spit during low tide.

stops.name: Bumpkin Island
stops.detail: Discover a quieter setting with slate beaches and remains of a stone farmhouse.

days.driving: Walking and ferry only; conditions vary based on sea state.
days.note: Treat these islands as separate options, not a connected public-ferry itinerary. No inter-island ferry service is currently operating; confirm authorized transport to each island before departure.

days.title: Coastal Gateway Exploration

stops.name: Grape Island
stops.detail: Enjoy a rustic walk through wooded trails and berry bushes near the shoreline.

stops.name: Hull Peninsula
stops.detail: Explore the maritime history of the gateway town and its views of the Atlantic.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for local Hull transit; ferry times vary by season.
days.note: Weekday ferry service is significantly reduced after Labor Day; confirm current dates.

intel.title: Urban Ferry Terminals
intel.text: Parking at Long Wharf is expensive and limited. Consider public transit or designated lots in Hingham or Hull for more predictable access.

intel.title: Island Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is generally available near the city but drops significantly on the outer islands. Do not rely on digital maps for navigation between trail markers.

intel.title: Supplies and Water
intel.text: There are no stores or reliable potable water sources on most islands. Carry all necessary food and water from the mainland.

intel.title: Ferry Boarding
intel.text: Arrive at least 30 minutes before your scheduled departure. Popular summer weekend slots can sell out despite having a reservation.

intel.title: Maritime Weather
intel.text: Fog or heavy swells can cause sudden ferry cancellations. Always have a mainland backup plan in case harbor transit is suspended.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at BOS and head to a waterfront hotel or gateway town. Verify ferry departure piers for your specific island itinerary.
plan.vehicle: Cars are for mainland travel only; islands are strictly pedestrian or bicycle (where allowed) via ferry.
plan.goldenHour: Spectacle Island offers prime sunset views of the Boston skyline, subject to ferry return schedules.
